 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Sunil Gupta, learned counsel for the appellant.

Shri K.K.Tiwari, learned Government Advo  respondent/State.
(1) Heard on I.A.No.9164/2022, which is first application filed under Section 389(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant -Ramesh.

(2) The appellant has been convicted for offence under Section 376 of IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment with fine of Rs.20,000/- and in default of payment of fine to further undergo 2 years simple imprisonment.
(3) The allegation against the appellant is that he committed rape upon the prosecutrix aged about 12 years, when she went to the jungle to graze the goats.
Accordingly, case has been registered against the appellant.
(4) Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the case.
He is in custody since 17.12.2012.
He is the only bread earner in the family.
There are so many omissions and contradictions in the statements of the prosecution witnesses.
There is no likelihood of hearing of the appeal in near future.
Hence, prays that the application for suspension of sentence be allowed and he be released on bail.
(5) Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State opposes the prayer for suspension of sentence and prays for its rejection.
(6) We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

(7) Looking to the statements of the prosecutrix Puja (PW-1) her mother Narbadabai (PW-2), the age of the prosecutrix who was 12 years at the time of incident and also the statement of Dr.Sudha Sharma (PW-5) who found injury on the private parts of the prosecutrix, bleeding from vagina and hymen was ruptured, no case is made out for suspension of sentence to the appellant.
